title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-05
source: flac16/48kHz; Source: Sony F995 > Sony TC-124 > Cassette Master > DAT (48k) - Recorded by Harry Ely and provided by Tim Dalton; Tansfer: Dat > Panasonic SV-3700 > Tascam DA-3000 > wav 16/48 - Transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav 16/48 > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope Ozone 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac1648; edited and mastered SIRMick April 2018

ai_review.summary: A clean 1969 audience tape that captures a solid late‑'69 Dead show with classic jams like It’s For the Other One and a standout China Cat > Rider segment.
ai_review.review: The recording is an unusually clear audience (AUD) capture for 1969, often praised as sounding better than many early ’70 tapes despite occasional taper sing‑along on Cosmic Charlie. The performance itself is a tasty slice of late‑’69 Dead, highlighted by the Other One sequence, Dancin’, China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, Uncle John → Main Ten and an early‑era Baby Blue, though the shorter early songs show the band’s lingering sloppiness.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers consistently note good to excellent sound quality for an audience tape and cite multiple standout jams, yielding a strong show rating; recording quality is also praised as above average for the era.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear for a 1969 AUD, better than most early tapes; occasional taper singing on Cosmic Charlie but overall crisp and well‑balanced with vintage gear.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid late‑'69 set that moves from a few sloppy short numbers into extended jams, giving the show a natural rise in energy and showcasing classic improvisational moments.
